plain.text: Dinah, the daughter of Leah and Jacob, went out to visit the women of the land. Shechem, the son of the local ruler Hamor, saw her, seized her and raped her. Afterwards he said he loved her and asked his father to get her for him as a wife. When Jacob's sons heard what had happened, they were deeply grieved and furious, because Shechem had done a disgraceful thing in Israel. Hamor and Shechem proposed that the two peoples intermarry and live together, and offered any bride-price they wanted.

Jacob's sons answered deceitfully. They said they could not give their sister to a man who was not circumcised, but if every male in the city were circumcised, they would become one people. Hamor and Shechem agreed and persuaded their city. Three days later, while the men were still in pain, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, took their swords, attacked the city and killed every male, including Hamor and Shechem. They took Dinah from Shechem's house. Jacob's sons looted the city. Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, "You have brought trouble on me by making me obnoxious to the people of this land." They replied, "Should he have treated our sister like a prostitute?"

summary.bigIdea: A terrible crime against Dinah is followed by deceit and violent revenge, showing how deeply broken this family and world are.
points: Her brothers deceive the city and take brutal revenge.
Jacob worries about the consequences; the brothers protest the wrong done to their sister.
summary.reflection: This is a painful story with no easy heroes. Why do you think the Bible includes stories like this?
